title: Quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed site of a space
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $M$ be a sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The module $M$ is quasi-coherent if, locally on this site, it has a presentation $R^{(I)}\to R^{(J_0)}\to M\to0$, with $I,J_0$ arbitrary small sets and the parentheses denoting coproducts in module sheaves. More explicitly, for every object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and such an exact presentation on each slice site $\mathcal C/U_i$, using the restricted ring sheaf. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an algebraic space $X$ over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], the category $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ is the full subcategory of module sheaves on $(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_X)$ satisfying this predicate.
